title: ProtoCharge: streaming smoothing + unbundled I/O minimums with security-Q alignment
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines a bounded experiment (ProtoCharge) to test a new hosted-API billing prototype that: 1) unbundles input vs output token metering with explicit per-direction rates; 2) introduces a streaming-smoothing credit mechanism (short-term buffer to avoid penalizing transient spikes); and 3) captures canonical answers to enterprise security questionnaire (SQ) items that affect minimums/contract language (data retention, KMS usage, audit log retention).

Why now:
Sales and enterprise legal have flagged repeated deal friction when minimums and streaming pricing are ambiguous for long-running chat/video transcription flows. Engineering telemetry shows many customers have bursty egress (output) token behaviour during multi-turn streaming sessions that leads to surprising invoices when minima apply snapback. Security/SQ answers also affect the minimums we can offer under Private/Dedicated vs Hosted (example: customers who require customer-managed KMS need a different minimum and SLA).

Objectives:
- Validate whether dual-rate metering (separate input/output prices) improves unit economics for both small, high-output apps and large low-latency low-output apps.
- Measure whether a streaming-smoothing credit (time-windowed amortization of bursty output) reduces invoice surprises while preserving revenue.
- Produce a canonical set of security-questionnaire answers and contract language snippets that map to pricing tiers/minimums and can be surfaced in sales playbooks.

Out of scope:
- Changes to Dedicated reserved-capacity contracts (this experiment only targets Hosted API customers).
- Full legal contract overhaul; we will produce suggested clause snippets for Legal review.
acceptance_criteria: Experiment config rolled out to a 5% traffic bucket on hosted API with dual-rate metering enabled (ingress_rate, egress_rate).
Streaming-smoothing credit implemented: 30s rolling window, credit up to 20% of instantaneous per-minute egress delta, configurable flag.
Billing simulations run on the last 90 days of anonymized tenant telemetry showing: delta in invoices (median, P90) and percent of customers whose monthly bill changes by >10%.
Security questionnaire companion doc completed with canonical answers and mappings to pricing tiers; Legal has acknowledged receipt and provided one round of feedback.
Playbook for Sales (pricing examples + migration FAQ) published to Drive and linked in experiment results.
plan: Design: finalize meter semantics (what counts as ingress vs egress; how tokens are attributed for partial-stream fragments). Owner: PM (Ava). Due: 2026-03-17.
Engineering: implement dual-rate meters and smoothing stub (feature flag gated). Owner: ENG-runtime team. Estimate: 5 pts. Due: 2026-03-31.
Billing: add simulation pipeline to replay token logs under new model and produce customer-level invoice deltas. Owner: Billing analytics. Due: 2026-04-05.
Security/Legal: complete SQ canonical answers doc and propose contract snippets on minimums tied to KMS/audit options. Owner: Security & Legal. Due: 2026-03-24.
Pilot: enable on 5% hosted traffic for 2 billing cycles & collect telemetry. Owner: PM + Ops. Start: 2026-04-01. Review: 2026-05-01.
Decision: recommend whether to adopt dual-rate + smoothing as opt-in toggle vs default, and publish postmortem with rollback thresholds.
metrics: % customers with bill delta >10% (before vs after) — target <5% for roll forward.
median token price per request (ingress-only vs egress-heavy) — monitor shifts by cohort.
support tickets mentioning "unexpected billing" attributable to minima — reduce by 30% in pilot cohort.
revenue delta (monthly) for pilot cohort — expected +2% to +8% depending on rate differential.
conversion lift/decline in trial-to-paid for sales-run deals where clarified pricing + SQ snippets used.
